### Morningstar Releases 2026 Medalist Ratings for 529 College Savings Plans, With 10 Upgrades and No Downgrades


November 9, 2026


*Four plans move up to Gold as Morningstar analysts find improvements across investment teams, oversight, and costs*


CHICAGO--(BUSINESS WIRE)--


[Morningstar](https://cts.businesswire.com/ct/CT?id=smartlink&url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.morningstar.com%2F&esheet=54638108&newsitemid=20261109135841&lan=en-US&anchor=Morningstar&index=1&md5=1c7427c87a2352aecc5148518978a4b0) , Inc. (Nasdaq: MORN), a leading provider of independent investment insights, today reveals the 2026 Morningstar Medalist Ratings™ for 60 of the nation’s most prominent 529 college savings plans.[The Morningstar Medalist Rating for 529 College Savings Plans](https://cts.businesswire.com/ct/CT?id=smartlink&url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.morningstar.com%2Fpersonal-finance%2Fmorningstar-529-ratings-best-plans&esheet=54638108&newsitemid=20261109135841&lan=en-US&anchor=The+Morningstar+Medalist+Rating+for+529+College+Savings+Plans&index=2&md5=df2f5968e7c62396f2e2af32a6153846) is a forward-looking assessment designed to help investors identify 529 plans that Morningstar analysts believe are best positioned to serve investors over the long term. Analysts evaluate the quality of a plan’s investment approach; the people managing it, state oversight, and costs, giving investors a way to compare plans beyond past performance. Plans receive one of five ratings: Gold, Silver, Bronze, Neutral, or Negative.


This year, Morningstar analysts assigned nine Gold ratings, 14 Silver ratings, 12 Bronze ratings, 19 Neutral ratings, and six Negative ratings. Gold ratings nearly doubled from five last year, and more than half of the plans (35 of 60) earned a Bronze rating or better. Analysts upgraded 10 plans, up from one in 2025, and downgraded none. These plans account for more than 90% of 529 industry assets, which surpassed $550 billion thus far in 2026.


"This year's ratings show how improvements behind the scenes can ultimately strengthen the choices available to education savers," said Hyunmin Kim, manager research senior analyst, Morningstar. "We're seeing examples of stronger investment teams, more robust state oversight, and thoughtful investment processes contributing to higher conviction from our analysts. With the cost of education continuing to rise, identifying high-quality plans remains an important part of helping families make informed savings decisions.”


The share of rated plans earning a Bronze rating or better rose 5 percentage points year over year (53% to 58%). All five plans that were Gold last year kept the rating, and four new Gold plans saw an upgrade from Silver in 2025. The five plans that maintained Gold ratings are Alaska's T. Rowe Price College Savings Plan, Illinois' Bright Start Direct-Sold College Savings Plan, Massachusetts' U.Fund College Investing Plan, the Pennsylvania 529 Investment Plan, and Utah's my529. Four plans moved up from Silver: California's ScholarShare College Savings Plan, Connecticut's CHET Direct College Savings Plan, Georgia's Path2College 529 Plan, and the Michigan Education Savings Program.


Stronger investment teams, and state oversight drove most of the boost in ratings. California, Georgia, and Michigan moved up due to TIAA-CREF, an investment manager that strengthened teams by adding analysts, and formalizing research processes, ultimately addressing concerns Morningstar raised last year about resources growing thin as its business expanded. Connecticut's State Treasurer’s office earned a higher oversight rating for stronger oversight and investment expertise.


Kansas' Quest529 Program and Schwab 529 College Savings Plan each moved up two rating levels, rising from Neutral in 2025 to Silver in 2026. Both plans changed investment managers from American Century to TIAA-CREF, helping lead to higher assessments from Morningstar analysts. The plans also became significantly less expensive. College Savings Iowa 529 Plan, and Invest529 rose from Bronze on stronger investment processes, and Wisconsin’s Edvest 529 Plan on a stronger team. North Carolina’s National College Savings Program jumped to Bronze, and Maine's NextGen College Investing Plan Connect also received its inaugural Morningstar Medalist Rating of Bronze.

**Morningstar’s 529 Rating Methodology**


Morningstar's[rating methodology for 529 plans](https://cts.businesswire.com/ct/CT?id=smartlink&url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.morningstar.com%2Ffunds%2Four-updated-529-medalist-rating-methodology-offers-more-detail-investors&esheet=54638108&newsitemid=20261109135841&lan=en-US&anchor=rating+methodology+for+529+plans&index=5&md5=4f0df7667f8b8e4d54f635d93eb25a7f) focus on each plan’s investment merits relative to its peers. The Process Pillar, weighted at 50%, examines investment quality as well as the rigor and resilience of the underlying investment process. The People and Parent Pillars are each weighted at 25%, equally highlighting the critical role of experienced management and effective state oversight. Plan fees are evaluated using modified z-scores that adjust a plan’s rating based on how its average expense ratio compares with the peer group median. The resulting Medalist Rating provides a holistic assessment of both investment quality and affordability.
